long_biography.plain_text:
A student engine design became a practical starting point for automotive engineer Ferdinand Piëch. At ETH Zurich, his thesis examined a twelve-cylinder racing engine with power taken from the centre of its crankshaft to limit vibration. His team later drew on that arrangement for the Porsche 917, joining two six-cylinder units to produce its racing engine.

He also taught students how technical ideas reach production. At Vienna University of Technology, his Innovation Management lectures explored the conditions that help new vehicle designs succeed. The programme also extended beyond the lecture room: accompanying vehicle exhibitions on Karlsplatz drew large audiences over several years.
